newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico kids sent home for sexy, gang clothes.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico kids sent home for sexy, gang clothes.

text.p: Hundreds of New Mexico high school students were sent home on Monday for wearing baggy pants, extra short shorts or revealing tops in a crackdown on sexy and gang-style clothing.

As students showed up for the first day of classes after the summer vacation, Albuquerque school officials checked them for offending articles like chains, see-through clothing, baggy pants, tank tops, shirts hanging below their fingertips or tops showing off their belly button.
Rick Murray, a spokesman for the Albuquerque Public School District, said about 200 students were sent home to change their clothes Monday morning.
The new dress code was introduced as part of efforts to curb gang activity and remind students that they are in school to learn, not flaunt their bodies.

"If pants are so baggy you can see underwear then it's a distraction to other students," said Robert Hennig, principal of the Sandia High School. "If students can't walk in them it's a safety hazard."
Many students said they would have to completely refit their wardrobes to come into line with the new dress code.
"All I have are baggy pants and tank tops," said Mary Brownell, 14, of Sandia High School, sporting a dog collar and spiky hair. "My mom's just going to have to take me shopping."

Hennig said his staff handed out T-shirts and pants to some students and told the parents of others to deliver a change of clothes. Those measures kept about 30 students in school who would otherwise have been sent home, he said.
